verdict.rationale: Open WebUI's 'computer' ecosystem docs show it can supervise real coding agents doing repo work: worktrees/workspaces per task, tool-approval cards showing every file read/edited with Allow/Deny, scheduled tasks like running test suites, and native backends for Codex/Claude Code/Cursor/Cline etc. This goes beyond chat snippets into actual agent supervision with file edits and test execution. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on community verification of the coding-agent supervision feature specifically (community evidence only covers RAG/UI complaints, not this workflow), and no evidence of direct git clone/repo-management primitives built into Open WebUI itself versus relying on the external agent's own tooling.
